name: units
description: Measurement tokens: the base grid and every spacing, radius, size, timing and breakpoint derived from it. A unit token may reference only another unit token, symbolically as {unit:cn-name}, never a raw var().

groups.comment: Base grid. Every spacing and radius decision derives from this.

cn-grid.note: 8px at the default root font size

groups.comment:
The measure: the widest a line of text is set, 67 characters of the base
paragraph. Stated in grid steps, not `ch`, which would resolve against
whatever font is rendering.

Measured: Lato's `0` advance is 0.58em, so 67ch at the 17px base is 41.29rem =
82.58 steps, rounded up. Changing the base face or its size makes this wrong.
For a consumer that wants "rounded" without choosing a step.
Control geometry: the visible pill, and the row it occupies.

cn-avatar-size-small.comment:
The identity mark's three diameters, in lines rather than grid units: a mark
sits beside text, so it measures in the text's leading. Both the mark and a
list's overflow count read them, which is why they are named here rather
than restated in each.

cn-avatar-size-large.note: 72px, standing for the profile itself; Cyan's one diameter

groups.comment:
Icon sizes: absolute lengths rather than grid multiples, following v20, which
files them beside the grid and marks them absolute.

cn-icon-size-xsmall.note: 16px at the default root font size

groups.comment:
Chrome is fixed and paints over the document, so a page insets its own
first line by the bar's depth rather than measuring it.

The depth an on-screen keyboard occupies at the block end. Chrome measures it
and publishes it here; `0px` is the value every browser gets until something
does, and the value a browser that shortens its own layout viewport keeps.

Stacking. Chrome rides above page content and Cyan's own fixed navigation,
and below the dialog, modal and snackbar layers Cyan still provides at 50000
and above. The tray's value resolves among chrome's parts, inside the box.

cn-z-chat-bar.comment: The authoring dock stands above the FAB and below a covering tray.

cn-z-scrim.comment: A covering tray stands above the bar and the FAB; its scrim immediately below it.

groups.comment: Interaction motion, shared by every control that answers a pointer.

The tray's two sizes. v20's values: a rail holds a compact chrome action's
seven-grid target with a one-and-a-half grid inset either side.

Breakpoints, in rem so a query follows a reader's enlarged default text.
A media or container query cannot read a custom property: a rule that
needs a threshold states the literal, and a test pins the literal here.

Each names the width where its band ends, and belongs to the band it ends:
small is the first and narrower, tablet is wider and narrower than the
second, desktop is the second and wider. `CnAppBar`'s `max-width: 38.75rem`
is that convention. The second is where a tray stands beside content
rather than over it.
